content: Cefpodoxime proxetil is prescribed for the treatment of patients with mild to moderate infections caused by susceptible strains of specific microorganisms in various clinical conditions. The recommended dosages, duration of therapy, and patient populations differ depending on the type of infection. Refer to the Dosage and Administration section for detailed guidance. Cefpodoxime proxetil is indicated for the treatment of acute otitis media caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae (excluding penicillin-resistant strains), Streptococcus pyogenes, Haemophilus influenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains), and Moraxella catarrhalis (including beta-lactamase-producing strains). It is also used for pharyngitis and/or tonsillitis caused by Streptococcus pyogenes. However, it is important to note that only intramuscular penicillin has been proven effective for the prevention of rheumatic fever. While cefpodoxime proxetil is generally effective in eradicating streptococci from the oropharynx, there is no evidence to support its use for the prophylaxis of subsequent rheumatic fever. Cefpodoxime proxetil is effective in treating community-acquired pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae or Haemophilus influenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains). It is also indicated for acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae (non-beta-lactamase-producing strains only), or Moraxella catarrhalis. However, there is insufficient evidence to establish its efficacy in treating acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis caused by beta-lactamase-producing strains of Haemophilus influenzae. Cefpodoxime proxetil is used to treat acute, uncomplicated urethral and cervical gonorrhea caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae (including penicillinase-producing strains). It is also effective for acute, uncomplicated ano-rectal infections in women caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae (including penicillinase-producing strains). However, its efficacy in treating rectal infections caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae in male patients has not been established. Additionally, cefpodoxime proxetil is not recommended for the treatment of pharyngeal infections caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae in either men or women. For uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections, cefpodoxime proxetil is effective against Staphylococcus aureus (including penicillinase-producing strains) and Streptococcus pyogenes. In cases of abscesses, surgical drainage should be performed as clinically indicated. Clinical trials have shown that the successful treatment of uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections is dose-dependent, with higher doses required compared to other recommended indications. Refer to the Dosage and Administration section for further details. Cefpodoxime proxetil is also indicated for acute maxillary sinusitis caused by Haemophilus influenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains), Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Moraxella catarrhalis. For uncomplicated urinary tract infections (cystitis), cefpodoxime proxetil is effective against Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Proteus mirabilis, and Staphylococcus saprophyticus. However, when considering cefpodoxime proxetil for the treatment of cystitis, its lower bacterial eradication rates should be weighed against the higher eradication rates and differing safety profiles of other approved agents. Refer to the Clinical Studies section for more information. Appropriate specimens for bacteriological examination should be obtained to isolate and identify the causative organisms and determine their susceptibility to cefpodoxime. Therapy may be initiated while awaiting the results of these studies. Once the results are available, antimicrobial therapy should be adjusted accordingly. To minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and maintain the effectiveness of cefpodoxime proxetil (marketed as VANTIN) and other antibacterial drugs, it should only be used to treat or prevent infections that are proven or strongly suspected to be caused by susceptible bacteria. When culture and susceptibility data are available, they should be considered in selecting or modifying antibacterial therapy.
